Hit rate = Hits / Total Accesses; miss rate = 1 − Hit rate.
Miss penalty = access time + data size / bandwidth.

concepts.name: SRAM vs. DRAM
facts: SRAM stores bits in a stable transistor circuit (6 transistors/bit, low retention power, used in caches/register files); DRAM stores bits as capacitor charge (1 transistor/bit, cheap, needs rewrite and refresh, used in DDR/GDDR/HBM).

concepts.name: Why DRAM Is Slow
facts: DRAM is slow because of weak storage signals, time-consuming sensing, destructive reads requiring restore, and large dense arrays with high RC delay.

Reading disturbs the stored charge so data must be restored after every row activation, and capacity-focused long rows/bitlines add RC delay; the solution is multi-bank, multi-rank DRAM.

Sensing takes time: sense amp amplifies a very small voltage change into a full 0/1
Destructive read: data must be restored after every row activation
Large dense arrays: long rows/bitlines have higher RC delay
Solution: multi-bank, multi-rank DRAM
